author: emmalrussell
body:
This PR updates `GithubApiClientAuthHelper` to use the [Hub4j Github API client ](https://github-api.kohsuke.org/) rather than the eclipse plugin client, which is no longer being updated on Maven. The latest version of Hub4j is using the new endpoints to get team information so should avoid the deprecated endpoints which caused some drama during [recent brownout](https://github.blog/changelog/2022-02-22-sunset-notice-deprecated-teams-api-endpoints/). 

Some points to note:

- I've found I needed to update PAT tokens used for OW API access to the latest format. 

- It seems that with the new client we just need user:email and read:org permission, not read:user as before. I think this is because the endpoints being used are a bit different to previous client. I've removed read:user from the scope set in the indirect client too. 

- Weirdly, when requests fail because of tokens not having the user:email scope, the exception you get is `GHFileNotFoundException`, which is derived from `IOException` (via `FileNotFoundException`). It seems odd, but I think it's by design - the docs for the client methods only specify `IOException` as the type of exception raised.

- If the token is invalid, an `HttpException` is thrown with status 401 when try to get user details.

- When the token does not have read:org scope there doesn't seem to be an exception at all, but `user.isMemberOf(org)` will return false even if user does belong to the org. 

You should be able to test this manually by changing default properties config to use github auth:
- use the following settings in src/config/default.properties:
auth_provider=github
auth_github_org=vimc-auth-test
auth_github_team=vimc-auth-team
auth_github_key=b9e2c4a9c3995ea43cd7
auth_github_secret=[ask me if you don't know this]
- Run up orderly web. You should see the big green 'Login with GitHub button'. You can either log in to github as yourself or as vimc-auth-test-user (see [auth.md](https://github.com/vimc/orderly-web/blob/master/docs/auth.md#authenticating-with-github) for password). If you're already logged in to github in the browser, you won't need to login again.
- I've added the vimc-auth-team to the vimc-auth-test org. If you're an admin in the org you should be able to add yourself and remove yourself from the team. I've added Lekan and Nick to this org.
- You should find that, when you're in the team, login to OW is successful; when you're not in the team, a message is displayed that you need to belong to the github org (maybe that should be updated to distinguish org from team - but anyway, login should be unsuccessful). 
- You can also check that login fails if auth_github_org is set to an org which you don't belong to e.g. 'hub4j'

body:
- Relates to #2172 feature request from github issues
- Built on top of #2081 since it provides signals with similar Device/Chip split.   

Adds support for LevelZero sysman performance factor signals and controls.  
Feature documentation [here](https://spec.oneapi.io/level-zero/latest/sysman/PROG.html#performance-factor)

The high level is that this is a unitless value in Sysman from 0-100 that provides a tradeoff between the compute hardware and all other hardware.  100 favors compute, 0 favors support hardware.  

In the Level IO Group we support reading the associated signals and writing controls for:
- [x] The Chip Level Compute Domain

Items keeping this in draft:
- [x] Updates to MockLevelZero.hpp
- [x] Updates to LevelZeroDevicePoolTest.cpp 
- [x] Updates to LevelZeroIOGroupTest.cpp
- [x] Update signals and controls for save/restore - setconfig() may not be granted, so getconfig() may not contain the last value written as outlined [here](https://spec.oneapi.io/level-zero/latest/sysman/api.html#zesperformancefactorsetconfig)

This fixes a regression in framework path discovery. It turns out that
either ClangImporter or other Swift module loaders can discover
additional framework search paths and add them to an existing
CompilerInvocation on the fly. When 70d2ba01 switched to directly
deserializing the compiler invocation it lost those additional
late-discovered framework paths from the module contexts.

author: chromium-wpt-export-bot
body:
Add support for break-before/after/inside rules for multi-line column
flex containers. Because we fragment the columns independently, we
needed a way to keep track of the break-after and early-break for each
column (tracked by NGFlexColumnBreakInfo).

We also may now have more than one early break in a given fragment, so
a way to pass in additional early breaks was added to the layout
algorithm when we abort due to an early break.

Because columns can be considered a "row" of columns, the break-before
for all first items in a column were accumulated to the container
(same with break-after and the last items in each column).

author: wyuka
body:
TICKET = LIKAFKA-43624
LI_DESCRIPTION =

When a controller re-election happens, the ReplicaStateMachine initializes the replicas with appropriate state -

1. If they are in the shutting down brokers list, or if the disk that the replica is on is marked as offline, then the replica is marked as OfflineReplica
1. Otherwise, they are initialized as OnlineReplica
 

Because shutting down brokers are persisted across different controllers (through ZK) in Linkedin's version of Kafka, hence replicas are being marked as offline even though they don't have any other nodes in the ISR. This is cause data to be unavailable for that partition.

 

This was observed in [GCN-36415](https://jira01.corp.linkedin.com:8443/browse/GCN-36415) and detailed in the document [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rSeJkTuVrBF1VAb0whAO0xTK1_qpcmJNhNeK5ePFvpQ/edit. ](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rSeJkTuVrBF1VAb0whAO0xTK1_qpcmJNhNeK5ePFvpQ/edit)The corresponding RCA ticket is [LIKAFKA-42499](https://jira01.corp.linkedin.com:8443/browse/LIKAFKA-42499).

 

We want to change the behavior so that replicas on shutting down brokers are not initialized to OfflineReplica, but rather to OnlineReplica.

Currently Sky only supports single task per DAG. This is an initial PR to run multiple independent tasks on Sky. One application enabled by this PR is racing benchmark where each task requires different accelerators. Potentially in the future we'll support general DAG on Sky.

@WoosukKwon and I are working together to finish this PR. Feel free to leave any comments or suggestions!

- [x] Support Python interface
```
with sky.Dag() as dag:
    task = []
    for acc in ['K80', 'V100']:
        task.append(sky.Task(run='nvidia-smi').set_resources(sky.Resources(accelerators={acc: 1})))
```
- [ ] Support YAML interface
- [ ] Cleanup output messages from different tasks
- [ ] Fix broken line breaks of messages
- [ ] Support terminating all tasks in DAG

author: basil
body:
`Security637Test` was relying on reflection to access a package-private field in `java.net.URL`, which is forbidden in Java 17. This was only being done in test code to verify some internal invariant, rather than production code. In one case the check was being done on an agent JVM, so I was able to add the necessary `--add-opens` flag when launching the agent. But in the other case the check was done in the Surefire test JVM, and adding `--add-opens` there would affect all other tests (which I didn't want to do), so I could think of no better option than to skip the test on Java 17 for that case.

author: jrray
body:
Add "mini-wrapper" for launching spk (and spawn)
    
    This new spk-launcher binary replaces what would normally be the "spk"
    binary entrypoint for spk. It currently can behave in "spk" mode or "spawn"
    mode, depending on the name of the binary. A suggested usage is to create
    a symlink like:
    
         /usr/local/bin/spk -> spk-launcher
    
    This is intended to allow running different versions of spk, for
    example running a development version to test out new features. A user
    would be expected to set $SPK_BIN_TAG to the name of a version. If this is
    not set, then the normally installed version in /opt/spk.dist is used.
    
    Setting SPK_BIN_TAG=test causes spk-launcher to check spfs for a platform
    tagged like "spk/spk-launcher/test" and will make a local copy of that platform's files
    under /dev/shm/spk/<platform digest>. If this path already exists then it
    is assumed to already be installed and the overhead of installing it is
    skipped. It will then set $SPK_BIN_PATH to
    /dev/shm/spk/<platform digest>/opt/spk.dist/spk and exec it.
    
    The script in bin/create-spk-platform is provided as a example of how to
    produce a new spfs platform suitable for use with the mini-wrapper.
